subject: Averaged asymptotic covariance matrix different in poolSat vs Chung & Cai method

messages.author: 62939dad0d7082c7
messages.subject: Averaged asymptotic covariance matrix different in poolSat vs Chung & Cai method
parts:
Hello, 

I am working through the code for implementing the MI2S method for categorical SEM proposed by Chung & Cai (2019). Thankfully, both Terrence J. and Lui and colleagues have provided ways to implement this method in R. 

In this process, I wanted to compare the results from poolSat function in lavaan.mi and the function that Lui et al. In many ways, the results from both methods were equivalent: averaged polychoric correlation matrices and averaged thresholds were the same, model fit statistics are the same, as were factor loadings, thresholds, variances, and R^2. 

However, the averaged asymptotic covariance matrix (of the polychoric correlations and the thresholds) produced by the two methods were quite different. As well the threshold SEs, z- and p-values, and CIs around the thresholds were markedly different; and the baseline model scaled Chi-square was quite different, too. For the ACM, the Lui et al method produced markedly smaller values compared to poolSat. 

So I am wondering about what might be causing this difference. I noticed in the scale.W command, the pooling procedure is based on Enders work. However, for the ACM, Chung & Cai provide a correction method specific to pooling these ACM matrices in the case of categorical variables. In Lui et al's code below, this correction is applied below the line "# Corrected variance-covariance matrix of the thresholds and the polychoric correlation matrix".

Would this correction account for the difference? And, because most of the model results were so similar across the board (very little difference in model fit statistics, factor loadings, threshold values), is this worrisome? 

Below is the code from the poolSat function and then below is the generic code that Lui et al provided as a supplement to their 2021 paper.

Thanks in advance,

Ian.

#### My code for the poolSat run
pooled <- poolSat(dat.ls.sub,
                  ordered = list.of.CAT.items, scale.W = TRUE,
                  omit.imps = c("no.conv", "no.se"))

#### Code for the Lui et al function
Get_ACM <- function(dat.ls, list.of.CAT.items, N, n){
  # OUTPUT VARS
  ACM.pcorr.threshold <- NULL
  ACM                 <- NULL
  pcorr.avg           <- NULL
  threshold.avg       <- NULL
 
  ## Get polychoric correlations, thresholds, and asymptotic covariance matrix
  lavCor.list <- lapply(dat.ls, function(x) {
    lavCor(x[,2:ncol(x)], ordered=list.of.CAT.items, output="full", se = "standard", baseline = FALSE)
  })
 
  # Average polychoric correlation matrix
  pcorr.list <- lapply(lavCor.list, function(x) (inspect(x, "est")$theta))
  M <- length(pcorr.list)
  pcorr.sum <- Reduce('+', pcorr.list)
  pcorr.avg <- pcorr.sum/length(pcorr.list)
  pcorr.avg.vec <- lavaan::lav_matrix_vech(pcorr.avg, diagonal = FALSE)
 
  # Average threshold matrix
  threshold.list <- lapply(lavCor.list, function(x) (inspect(x, "est")$tau))
  threshold.sum <- Reduce('+', threshold.list)
  threshold.avg <- threshold.sum/length(threshold.list)
  threshold.avg <- as.numeric(threshold.avg)
  attr(threshold.avg, "th.idx") <- lavInspect(lavCor.list[[1]], "th.idx") # add attribute to thresholds
 
  avg.sampstat <- c(threshold.avg, pcorr.avg.vec)
 
  sampstat.list<-mapply(function(x,y) {c(x,lavaan::lav_matrix_vech(y, diagonal = FALSE))},
                        threshold.list,
                        pcorr.list,
                        SIMPLIFY=FALSE)
 
  # Between-imputation variance of the thresholds and the polychoric correlation matrix
  satACOV.pcorr.threshold.between.list <- lapply(sampstat.list, function(x) {
    (x-avg.sampstat)%*%t(x-avg.sampstat)
  })
  satACOV.pcorr.threshold.between.sum <- Reduce('+', satACOV.pcorr.threshold.between.list)
 
  # Average within-imputation asymptotic covariance matrix of
  # the thresholds and the polychoric correlation matrix using using lavaan
  satACOV.pcorr.threshold.within.list <- lapply(lavCor.list, vcov)
  satACOV.pcorr.threshold.within.sum <- Reduce('+', satACOV.pcorr.threshold.within.list)
  satACOV.pcorr.threshold.within.avg <- satACOV.pcorr.threshold.within.sum/length(satACOV.pcorr.threshold.within.list)
  # Sort - thresholds come first
  thr.idx <- grepl("\\|",colnames(satACOV.pcorr.threshold.within.avg))
  Sort <- c(which(thr.idx), which(!thr.idx))
  satACOV.pcorr.threshold.within.avg <- satACOV.pcorr.threshold.within.avg[Sort, Sort]
 
  # Corrected variance-covariance matrix of the thresholds and the polychoric correlation matrix
  ACM.pcorr.threshold <- N*(satACOV.pcorr.threshold.within.avg + satACOV.pcorr.threshold.between.sum*(M+1)/((M-1)*M))
  # ACM.pcorr.threshold_Adj <- N*(satACOV.pcorr.threshold.within.avg*(N-1)/N +
  #                                 satACOV.pcorr.threshold.between.sum*(M+1)/((M-1)*M))
  # ACM.pcorr.threshold_Adj is in line with fitting a CFA model to each imputed dataset using WLS
  #     and getting the variance-covariance matrix of sample statistics from the lavaan output
  #     for the within-impuation variance-covariance matrix
 
  npara.sampstat <- nrow(ACM.pcorr.threshold)
 
  # Corrected variance-covariance matrix of the polychoric correlation matrix only
  ACM <- ACM.pcorr.threshold[(npara.sampstat-(n*(n-1)/2)+1):npara.sampstat,
                             (npara.sampstat-(n*(n-1)/2)+1):npara.sampstat]
 
  OUTPUT <- list(ACM.pcorr.threshold = ACM.pcorr.threshold,
                 ACM                 = ACM,
                 pcorr.avg           = pcorr.avg,
                 threshold.avg       = threshold.avg)
  OUTPUT
}

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Averaged asymptotic covariance matrix different in poolSat vs Chung & Cai method
parts: I noticed in the scale.W command
If you set that FALSE, are the results more similar?
the pooling procedure is based on Enders work
My code cites his book for formulas, but I think the formulas were derived earlier (see his book for citations).
However, for the ACM, Chung & Cai provide a correction method specific to pooling these ACM matrices in the case of categorical variables

What do they state in their paper is different about categorical variables?  From my recollection, they simply applied Rubin's rules (the multiparameter version), which has nothing to do with what the parameters are.
Would this correction account for the difference?

No idea what the differences actually are, but it could have something to do with whether they used N or N - 1 (the latter remaining unnecessarily common in SEM literature, due to its use in SEM software developed decades ago that used Wishart likelihoods).  Or perhaps you are comparing their ACM to the NACOV returned by lavaan (which is N times the ACOV or ACM).
